Which of the following best weakens the argument that the new policy will reduce traffic?

Re: weakens question

posted by QStarter Jan 1, 2020

City planners argue that the new congestion charge will reduce traffic in the downtown core. They assume that price will deter drivers.

Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the argument?

(A) The charge is collected automatically by camera.

(B) Most downtown drivers receive a parking reimbursement that fully offsets the charge.

(C) The city has tested a similar charge in another district.

(D) Public transit ridership has been declining for five years.

(E) The mayor supports the policy.

Re: weakens question

posted by Expert Jan 2, 2020

The conclusion: the charge will reduce traffic. The assumption: price deters drivers. To weaken, attack the assumption — show that drivers are insulated from the price. (B) does exactly that. Answer: B.

Re: weakens question

posted by Student Jan 3, 2020

I narrowed it to B and D. D is a trend, not a counter to the mechanism, so B.

Official Answer: B
